title: Keyboard, mouse & trackpad
blurb: Keys typing wrong, mouse frozen, trackpad not clicking, touch screen.

remedies.title: Keyboard types the wrong characters
remedies.why: A different keyboard layout is active; a shortcut (Alt+Shift or Windows+Space on Windows, Control+Space on Mac) switches it.

steps.text: Press Windows+Space to cycle layouts, and check the language shown next to the clock.
Remove layouts you don't use: Settings › Time & language › Language & region › your language › Options › Keyboards.
Click the input menu (flag/letters) in the menu bar and pick the right layout.
Remove layouts you don't use: Keyboard › Text Input › Edit.
If numbers come out instead of letters on a small laptop, Num Lock is on: press Fn+Num Lk.

remedies.title: Some keys don't work, or the keyboard stopped
remedies.why: Filter Keys or Sticky Keys is on, a key is physically stuck, a wireless keyboard's battery is flat, or the driver failed.

steps.text: Try the On-Screen Keyboard to keep working meanwhile.
Turn off Filter Keys and Sticky Keys: Settings › Accessibility › Keyboard.
Turn off Slow Keys and Sticky Keys: Accessibility › Keyboard.
Wireless: replace batteries or charge, then re-pair or replug the USB receiver.
Blow out crumbs at an angle with compressed air.
Device Manager › Keyboards › uninstall the keyboard › restart.

remedies.title: Mouse pointer frozen, jumpy or not moving
remedies.why: A flat battery, a dirty or shiny surface, the USB receiver too far away, or the computer itself frozen.

steps.text: If the keyboard still works (Caps Lock light changes), the computer is fine: focus on the mouse.
Replace batteries or charge; move the USB receiver to a port nearer the mouse (a front port or extension).
Use a mouse mat; glass and glossy desks confuse the sensor.
Try another USB port, or another mouse to rule the computer out.
Check the pointer speed: Mouse settings.
Check tracking speed in Mouse settings.

remedies.title: Trackpad or touchpad not working
remedies.why: The touchpad was turned off (often with an Fn key), it turns off when a mouse is plugged in, or its gestures changed.

steps.text: Press the touchpad key (Fn + a key with a touchpad icon).
Turn the touchpad on, and check "Leave touchpad on when a mouse is connected".
Check Trackpad settings: Tap to click, scroll direction and gestures.
Accessibility › Pointer Control › turn off "Ignore built-in trackpad when mouse or wireless trackpad is present".
A swollen battery can push the trackpad up so it won't click: if the case bulges, stop using it and get it checked.

remedies.escalate: If the case bulges or the trackpad lifts, stop using the laptop and tell IT (swollen battery).

remedies.title: Scrolling goes the wrong way
remedies.why: "Natural" scrolling moves the page with your fingers, like a phone; some prefer the opposite.

steps.text: Touchpad: Scrolling direction. Mouse: the maker's software.
Trackpad › Scroll & Zoom › Natural scrolling (it also changes the mouse).

remedies.title: Mouse double-clicks on one click (or single clicks open things)
remedies.why: A worn mouse switch registers twice, or the system is set to open items on one click.

steps.text: Try another mouse; if the problem goes, the first mouse's button is worn.
Folder options › General › choose "Double-click to open an item".
Set the double-click speed in Mouse properties.
Set the double-click speed in Accessibility › Pointer Control.

remedies.title: Touch screen doesn't respond or touches by itself
remedies.why: The touch driver is off or needs a reset; dirt or a charger can cause ghost touches.

steps.text: Clean the screen; unplug the charger to see if ghost touches stop.
Device Manager › Human Interface Devices › HID-compliant touch screen: Enable, or Disable and Enable again.
Calibrate: Control Panel › Tablet PC Settings › Calibrate (if present).

remedies.title: Everything types in capitals, or a modifier key seems stuck
remedies.why: Caps Lock or Sticky Keys is on, or a remote session left a key pressed.

steps.text: Tap Caps Lock, then press and release Shift, Ctrl, Alt (Option) and Windows (Command) once each.
Turn off Sticky Keys.
Turn off Sticky Keys in Accessibility › Keyboard.
If you just used Remote Desktop, close it; keys can stay "pressed" until you do.
